title: Predicting brain tumor recurrence: development and validation of a DNA-methylation based nomogram in meningioma

publications.title: DNA methylation profiling to predict recurrence risk in meningioma: development and validation of a nomogram to optimize clinical management

institution: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, University Health Network, Toronto (International Consortium on Meningiomas, multi-institutional)
platform: Illumina (array type unspecified in live metadata)
needs_manual_review_reason: DEEP-AUDIT UPDATE (2026-07-14): (1) publications[0].authors was truncated to exactly 6 names; expanded to the full 24-entry Europe PMC authorString for PMID 31158293 (Nassiri F ... International Consortium on Meningiomas, Zadeh G, Aldape KD), including the group-author entry as PubMed lists it. (2) corresponding_author corrected from 'Farshad Nassiri / Kenneth D. Aldape' to 'Kenneth D. Aldape / Gelareh Zadeh'. Verified directly against the paper's own correspondence footnote (full text, PMC6620635, fetched via NCBI efetch since Europe PMC's affiliation-derived corresponding-author scan returned nothing usable for this record): '<corresp id="c1"><bold>Corresponding Author:</bold> Kenneth D. Aldape, National Cancer Institute...(kenneth.aldape@nih.gov); Gelareh Zadeh, MacFeeters-Hamilton Center for Neuro-Oncology Research...(gelareh.zadeh@uhn.ca).</corresp>'. Nassiri F is the first author, not a corresponding author per this footnote; he was previously included by author-list-position assumption, exactly the pattern this audit was asked to catch. (3) has_outcome_data corrected from 'Not reported' to true (tags.has_outcome_data likewise true). The prior note reasoned that per-sample recurrence/outcome data was not confirmed as deposited in EGA's public sample metadata and therefore could not be marked true; however, the paper's own full text (PMC6620635 abstract/results) directly reports recurrence-free-survival (RFS) outcome analysis for this exact study cohort: 'a methylome model of 5-year recurrence-free survival (RFS)...independently associated with RFS...(hazard ratio 3.6, 95% CI: 1.8-7.2, P<0.001)...resulted in 2 groups with distinct recurrence patterns (hazard ratio 7.7, 95% CI: 5.3-11.1, P<0.001)'. This is exactly the failure pattern flagged for this audit (full-text outcome data present but left 'Not reported' because only repository metadata was checked); has_outcome_data is now set true since RFS/outcome data is demonstrably present for this cohort's samples, even though it is not separately exposed as an EGA sample-metadata field. molecular_subtype_annotated left unchanged (false) since the paper reports a continuous methylome recurrence-risk SCORE/nomogram, not a discrete named subtype classification system. NEW RECORD (2026-07-11). Note the unusual dataset accession format flagged in the task: EGAD00010001687 (an 'EGAD0001-' prefixed metadata-only/array-style dataset accession rather than the more common 'EGAD00001-' file-based prefix) was double-checked and resolves correctly live via the standard /datasets/{accession}/... endpoints; title 'Methylation', description 'Meningioma Methylation', num_samples=280, technologies=['Illumina'] (no more specific array chemistry given, e.g. 450K vs. EPIC, hence modality confidence Medium and platform left partially unspecified). Live /samples endpoint confirms 280 unique subject_id values (no duplicates), all phenotype='meningioma', with subject_id prefixes revealing a 3-site multi-institutional cohort: MDA=140, TOR=122, HK=18 (consistent with the paper's 'International Consortium on Meningiomas' multi-site design and author list spanning Toronto/MD Anderson-style and Hong Kong collaborators). No PMID is attached in the live EGA record (pubmed_ids=null); the paper (PMID 31158293, Nassiri et al. 2019, Neuro-Oncology) was located via web search matching the EGA study's title verbatim ('Predicting brain tumor recurrence: development and validation of a DNA-methylation based nomogram in meningioma' is the EGA title; the published paper's title is a near-identical 'DNA methylation profiling to predict recurrence risk in meningioma: development and validation of a nomogram to optimize clinical management'), high confidence given the exact match of study aim, first author, and sample-ID site-code structure. RULE 13 APPLIED STRICTLY: although this paper's entire premise is predicting per-sample 5-year recurrence-free survival from methylation profiles, the live /samples endpoint exposes only phenotype='meningioma' for every entry, with no recurrence, RFS, or outcome field of any kind in the public EGA metadata. Per this project's explicit rule against inferring has_outcome_data/recurrence_annotated from a paper's title or abstract alone, both has_outcome_data and recurrence_annotated are left 'Not reported'/false here; the underlying per-sample clinical/outcome annotations almost certainly exist in the paper's own supplementary tables but are not confirmed as deposited in the public EGA sample-level metadata itself, so cannot be marked true under this project's verification standard. This cohort may partially or wholly overlap with existing inventory records from the same Nassiri/Zadeh Toronto group (mng-utoronto-2021-genomic.json, gse-180061-methylation.json, egad00001007494-nassiri-rnaseq.json), which derive from the later 2021 Nature integrative-classification paper; this 2019 Neuro-Oncology nomogram cohort (n=280, 3-site consortium) predates and is structured differently (multi-institutional recurrence-prediction cohort vs. single-institution classification cohort) from that later work, so it is NOT merged with those records here, but patient overlap across the two Toronto-led projects is plausible and should be checked centrally. Only public EGA study/dataset-level metadata was used; the controlled-access data itself was never accessed, per docs/scope.md. CROSS-COHORT AUDIT (2026-07-11): reviewed as part of a corpus-wide dedup and cross-link audit. Specific evidence found: the Toronto-site subset of this 280-sample 3-site cohort is 122 samples (site prefix 'TOR'), numerically close to the 121-patient single-institution cohort in mng-utoronto-2021-genomic.json / gse-180061-methylation.json, with the same corresponding authors (Nassiri/Zadeh/Aldape), same institution, and the same modality (DNA methylation array). This is suggestive of possible patient overlap but the public EGA sample-level metadata for this accession exposes no specimen/subject identifiers comparable to the 'CAM20.xxxx'-style IDs that were used to directly confirm the GSE168726/GSE180061 duplicate elsewhere in this corpus, so patient-level overlap cannot be confirmed or ruled out from public metadata alone. possible_duplicate_needs_verification corrected to true (previously false, which did not match this record's own 'flagged for centralized dedup check' language) so this stays visible as unresolved and pending EGA controlled-access sample-ID comparison in a future pass; not treated as a confirmed duplicate and not merged or cross-linked.
duplicate_notes: Possible cohort overlap with mng-utoronto-2021-genomic.json / gse-180061-methylation.json / egad00001007494-nassiri-rnaseq.json (same Toronto PI group, Nassiri/Zadeh/Aldape), but this is an earlier (2019), larger, 3-site consortium cohort (Toronto+MD Anderson-style+Hong Kong) rather than the single-institution 2021 Nature integrative classification cohort; not confirmed as the same patients, flagged for centralized dedup check rather than assumed. Flag kept/corrected to true (unresolved) pending future controlled-access-level sample-ID comparison; not merged or cross-linked absent stronger evidence.
